01.reason: Hezekiah fell ill and Isaiah set up an academy at his door: a brief narrated event about biblical figures, offered as exegesis of a verse.

02.reason: A bare report that Jonah's wife made the pilgrimage and was not reprimanded, cited as legal evidence; nothing follows from it.

03.reason: A report of the practices of Michal and Jonah's wife, cited as proof in a legal argument; there is no incident and nothing follows.

04.reason: A one-line report that Joshua laid out roads, used to explain a legal status; it is a bare report about a biblical figure, not a narrative.

05.reason: Homiletic exegesis of how God built Eve; there is no narrated incident.

06.reason: An eyewitness statement about the size of a place, cited as evidence in a halakhic objection; nothing happens and no one responds.

07.reason: An eschatological teaching about Abraham raising sinners from Gehenna: a general description, not an event that happened.
